Anna — really useful detail, thanks. Short answer / recommended path up front: start with a brief Hosted API pilot to validate correctness and end-to-end latency under real payloads, then transition to Dedicated reserved capacity for production (or Private only if your legal/compliance team requires an on-prem/VPC-only deployment).

Why this order?
- Hosted pilot: fastest to iterate (no infra procurement), lets us collect real telemetry (token distribution, tail latency) and tune batching/KV caching. We can run a 2-week pilot at your realistic QPS and measure 99p under live conditions.
- Dedicated for production: gives predictable throughput, data isolation at the infra layer, and SLA-backed latency targets. With Dedicated we can allocate a reserved GPU pool sized for sustained 100 qps and configured autoscaling for spikes; that delivers much better 99p stability than a naive hosted multi-tenant setup.
- Private VPC/on-prem: recommended only if procurement/legal require data to never touch hosted control planes. Operational overhead and lead time are higher.

Immediate asks from our side so we size the pilot/dedicated recommendation:
1) Confirm sustained baseline (80–120 qps) and spike pattern (350 qps — how long do spikes last?).
2) Share a representative sample payload and expected average response token size (you mentioned ~1.8k output).
3) Any hard constraints on encryption or key management (KMS/HSM).

Looping in Olga and Kimberly to outline the config and provide an initial benchmark estimate (see attached file names they’ll send). Next step from our side: we’ll propose a 2-week Hosted pilot plan and a follow-on Dedicated sizing + cost estimate.

Can we schedule a 30-min alignment early next week? I’m available Mon/Tue mornings PT.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Anna — thanks for the detailed traffic profile. A few concrete notes and an initial config suggestion below. I included two attachments: latency_benchmarks_99th.csv (synthetic 99p numbers across instance classes) and pilot_config_suggestion.yaml (suggested pilot parameters).

Quick mapping from your numbers to deployment choices:
- Target: sustained 100 qps, spike to 350 qps (spikes ~10–20 mins, once per hour).
- Tokens: ~3.3k total roundtrip (1.5k in + 1.8k out).
- 99th latency target interactive <=200ms: this is aggressive for that token size unless you accept a specialized Dedicated pool with optimized KV caching and aggressive batching windows.

Suggested pilot approach (practical, low lift):
1) Hosted API pilot (2 weeks): run at shadow/limited production traffic (20–30% of your calls) to collect live token distribution and tail latency. Use streaming responses disabled initially to measure full response times.
   - Pilot config: concurrency cap 60, target baseline 30–50 qps, enable KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, warm-up phase 2 hours.
2) Parallel Dedicated sizing test (lab): we’ll spin a Dedicated test pool using 8xA100-equivalent nodes with continuous batching optimizations to capture 99p numbers for your payload (we’ll run synthetic replays). This gives us a realistic projection for production sizing and cost.

Initial numbers from internal microbenchmarks (see attached CSV):
- Hosted (multi-tenant): 99p ~ 380–520ms at 100 qps for 3k tokens (wide variance).
- Dedicated prototype (8x reserved, optimized batching): 99p ~ 120–200ms at sustained 100 qps with sub-second spikes to 350 qps if autoscaling + burst pool enabled.

Security/compliance notes:
- Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and per-tenant audit logs. That satisfies SOC2 evidence requirements in nearly all cases we’ve encountered — we’ll provide SOC2 artifacts during procurement.
- Private VPC/on-prem remains the option if legal requires isolated control plane or air-gapped deployments.

Next steps I can action:
- Attach pilot config file and a short runbook for the 2-week Hosted run.
- Schedule the Dedicated lab replay after we have a representative payload.
- Generate a preliminary cost estimate and PO-ready quote (Kimberly, can you prepare the estimate and a brief statement of work?).

Olga Petrov
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
